title: [RAWTHROW][15] torch/csrc/jit/tensorexpr: 294 conversions, the burn-down list is empty
body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack/tree/0.15.0) (oldest at bottom):
* __->__ #198500
* #198268
* #198231

## Author Notes

Bulk migration of tensorexpr.

## Agent Notes

Written by Claude Code:

> The last burn-down entry: removes `'torch/csrc/jit/tensorexpr/**'` from
> RAWTHROW's `exclude_patterns`, together with the "Burned down later in this
> stack" block it was the last member of. What remains are the seven permanent
> entries (vendored code, forks, and the c10-free qnnpack headers).
>
> 294 raw throws in 35 files under `torch/csrc/jit/tensorexpr` (NNC) become
> `TORCH_CHECK`. 208 of them threw NNC's own classes from `exceptions.h`
> (`malformed_input` 118, `unsupported_dtype` 54, `malformed_ir` 21,
> `unimplemented_lowering` 14, `out_of_range_index` 1), the rest
> `std::runtime_error` (82) and `std::logic_error` (4). Where an `if` guarded
> the throw and held nothing else, it is collapsed into the check, and
> if/else-if chains in which every branch threw become the same checks in
> sequence (176 sites). The other 118 are `TORCH_CHECK(false, ...)` in
> `default:`/`else` branches or in if/else-if chains that also have
> non-throwing branches.
> Three of the collapses are inside `TYPE_CASE`/`VALUE_AS_*DISPATCH` macros,
> where clang-format then realigns the whole macro's backslash column; those
> hunks are larger than the change in them.
>
> **Messages are byte-identical.** Each NNC class prefixed its `what()` with
> its category and pretty-printed the IR node it was handed, so each site
> spells out exactly what the constructor used to build:
>
> ```
> throw malformed_input("bad dtype in CompareSelect", v);
> TORCH_CHECK(..., "MALFORMED INPUT: bad dtype in CompareSelect - ", std::to_string(v));
> ```
>
> `std::to_string` rather than passing `v` to `c10::str` is load-bearing:
> there is no `operator<<` for `ExprPtr`/`StmtPtr`, so `c10::str(v)` would
> print a pointer. `exceptions.h` itself is untouched: nothing in-tree throws
> those five classes any more, but it is a public `TORCH_API` header and
> deleting them is not throw-handling.
>
> **Exception types.** Python-visible: `RuntimeError` before and after, on
> both paths. The `HANDLE_TH_ERRORS` path already flattened every
> `std::exception`, and the bare pybind bindings in `tensorexpr_init.cpp` map
> `std::runtime_error` and `c10::Error` both to `RuntimeError`. The NNC
> classes derive from `std::runtime_error`, so `out_of_range_index` was a
> `RuntimeError`, not an `IndexError`, and becomes plain `TORCH_CHECK`, not
> `TORCH_CHECK_INDEX`. `std::logic_error` has no distinct pybind mapping
> either (established in `[12]`). C++-visible: `std::runtime_error` becomes
> `c10::Error`, which is the "fine for TorchScript" decision already applied
> in `[10]`-`[12]`. There are no C++ NNC tests left (`test/cpp/tensorexpr`
> went in #158928), and no Python test matches on these types or messages.
>
> **One catch had to move with them.** `evalInt` (`eval.cpp`) caught
> `std::runtime_error` and returned `nullopt`, and its only caller,
> `FunctionInliner` (`loopnest.cpp`), relies on that `nullopt` to decline
> inlining a producer whose store index is neither a `Var` nor a constant. The
> evaluator throws "could not find Var in context" for such an index (and
> the converted dtype checks in `eval.h`, `ir.h` and `types.h` sit on the same
> path), so after the conversion those would have escaped `evalInt` and
> `computeInline` would throw instead of declining; `TensorExprKernel`'s
> `catch (...)` would not mask it because fallback is off by default. The catch is widened to
> `const std::exception&`. One side effect: the pre-existing
> `TORCH_CHECK(rhs != 0, "Division by zero")` in the same evaluator used to
> escape this catch and now also becomes `nullopt`, i.e. the inliner declines
> instead of throwing for an index that divides by a constant zero.
>
> **Code no build here compiles.** `llvm_codegen.cpp` (29 sites) is under
> `TORCH_ENABLE_LLVM`, and nothing in OSS CI sets `USE_LLVM`, so it is only
> compiled internally. `cuda_codegen.cpp`/`.h` (18) are compiled by CUDA CI
> but not by the local CPU build. Those were reviewed line by line instead.
>
> Test Plan:
>
> ```
> spin lint -- --skip CLANGTIDY
> spin lint -- --take RAWTHROW --all-files
> bash -ic 'BUILD_CONFIG spin develop'
> python test/test_tensorexpr.py
> python test/test_tensorexpr_pybind.py
> python test/test_jit_fuser_te.py
> python test/test_static_runtime.py
> ```
>
> plus a positive control for the `evalInt` catch: a script that builds a
> producer storing to `A[i + 1]` and calls `LoopNest.compute_inline(A)`
> declines without raising, and with only the catch reverted it raises
> `RuntimeError: MALFORMED INPUT: could not find Var in context - i`.
>
> This change was authored with the help of an AI assistant (Claude Code).

cc @EikanWang @jgong5
